children: , the commercial and defense engine manufacturer, won a rare vote of confidence from across the industry after Honeywell Aerospace's chief executive said its planned castings acquisition could be positive for the broader aerospace supply chain, according to Reuters. GE shares climbed approximately 3.1% to $316.59, based on the latest quote shown, versus the earlier $312.42 reading. The valuation picture is getting richer, too: the shares trade 16.74% above the $271.20 GF Value, suggesting investors are already pricing in a meaningful amount of future execution.

GE is paying $11.75 billion for Consolidated Precision Products, a producer of cast components used in jet engines and other high-stress applications. The financing mix is substantial but manageable on paper: $7 billion will come from cash, with the balance funded through new debt. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027, assuming regulators sign off. The strategic attraction is straightforward. Aerospace manufacturers have spent years wrestling with supply-chain constraints, and bringing more critical casting capacity under GE's roof could give the company greater control over one of the industry's stubborn production bottlenecks.

The bigger question is whether that control will justify the price. GE generated $3 billion of free cash flow in the second quarter, putting the acquisition value at roughly 3.9 times that single quarter's cash generation. That gives GE financial firepower, but investors still have to weigh integration risk, additional leverage and the premium already embedded in the stock. Honeywell's endorsement strengthens the industrial case for the deal. It does not settle the valuation debate.

title: GE Aerospace Gains Over 3.1% as a Rival Validates Its $11.75 Billion Bet
